item.prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

For the fair, Ana did an ____ to see which soil helps beans grow fastest.
choices: expirement
experement
expiriment
experiment
item.spelling_pattern: unstressed vowels in the second and third syllables (ex-per-i-ment)

student_error.expiriment: spells the unclear second vowel with i, as it sounds in 'expire'
student_error.experement: spells the unstressed third vowel with e, matching the e's around it
student_error.expirement: makes both vowel swaps, the very common 'expire' misspelling

item.explanation: Experiment is spelled ex-per-i-ment. Expiriment changes the first e to i, experement changes the i to e, and expirement does both.

item.prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

Grandpa's ninetieth birthday party was a special ____ for our whole family.
choices: ocasion
occasion
ocassion
occassion
item.spelling_pattern: doubled consonants: double c but single s in occasion

student_error.ocasion: does not hear the double c, so writes the k sound with one c
student_error.occassion: doubles the s as well as the c, expecting both consonants to be doubled
student_error.ocassion: remembers that one consonant is doubled but doubles the wrong one, the s instead of the c

item.explanation: Occasion has a double c and a single s: oc-ca-sion. Ocasion drops one c, occassion doubles the s, and ocassion does both, putting the double letter on the wrong consonant.

choices: embarased
embarrased
embarassed
embarrassed
item.spelling_pattern: two sets of double consonants: rr and ss

student_error.embarassed: keeps the double s but writes one r
student_error.embarrased: keeps the double r but writes one s

item.prompt:

Being the line leader for the whole week felt like a real ____ to Sam.
choices: priviledge
privilege
priveledge
privelege
item.spelling_pattern: unstressed i in the second syllable, and -lege with no d

student_error.privelege: spells the unstressed second vowel with e, matching the e's later in the word
student_error.priviledge: adds a d, spelling the ending like 'knowledge' or 'ledge'

item.explanation: Privilege is spelled priv-i-lege with no d. Privelege changes the i to e, priviledge adds a d, and priveledge does both.

choices: permenant
permanant
permanent

item.spelling_pattern: unstressed a in the middle syllable and the -ent (not -ant) ending

student_error.permenent: spells the unclear middle vowel with e, matching the other e's
student_error.permanant: confuses -ent with -ant, repeating the a of the middle syllable

item.explanation: Permanent is per-ma-nent. Permenent changes the a to e, permanant ends in -ant, and permenant does both.
